A larger joint budget can admit more reports and reduce the minimum risk. It can also shift detail from one
domain to another. Here B has targets (0,0), while A has (1,1), (−1,1), or (1,−1), with probabilities
1−3k/20, k/20, and k/10. The choices k=0, 1, and 2 set the probability of a reversal in each fictional distribution.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Tighter joint budget.** At k=1 and cap 3/40, the unique optimum discloses A ahead only in S. Its risk is 1/5,
  joint-event probability 1/20, and occupied-grade counts (2,1).
- **Larger joint budget.** Raising the cap to 1/8 admits the report that states a direction only in C. It has
  risk 11/80 and joint-event probability 1/10. With more weight on C, the best report now uses two grades
  in C and one in S, giving counts (1,2).
- **Both domains disclosed.** At cap 3/20, the double-positive card becomes feasible at equality. Its risk is
  7/80, joint-event probability 3/20, and occupied-grade counts (2,2). The cap is inclusive.
- **More posterior reversals.** With k=2 and cap 3/20, the best report again states a direction only in S,
  at risk 17/80 and joint-event probability 1/10. Changing k changes the distribution. Compare budgets
  within a fixed k to isolate the effect of the budget.

The chart counts the grades used in S and C. The grade table gives each site's two grades. At every budget,
the app lists all reports tied for the lowest risk and plots the counts for the first of those reports.
At k=1 and zero budget, all directions are withheld at risk 1/4. At k=0, both directions can be stated
even at zero budget, with risk zero.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
All settings use the same nine cards, weights (1/4,3/4), and withholding costs (1/4,1/4). The joint event
occurs if either domain has an error share above zero. Expected-error caps are disabled. A shared grade
withholds a direction, and the error share is undefined when the report states no directions in a domain.
The calculation is exact for the fictional distributions specified here.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
The [R script](../../data/recipes/profile-resolution.R) reproduces the candidates, tied optima, and frontiers
for all twenty-one settings with postrank 1.2.0 and gmp.

```r
source("profile-resolution.R")
result <- profile_resolution()
result$summary
```
:::

Source: [postrank multidomain decisions](https://joonho112.github.io/postrank/articles/mdomain-decisions.html).
